label: input token 0 during copy phase (or at t=0)
explanation: Fires when the input token is the digit 0 being fed back during the copy phase (relative activation ~0.7-1.0; the first of two consecutive copied 0s is typically ~1.0, the second ~0.8), and weakly (~0.27) when 0 is the very first original token (t=0). Does NOT fire on 0 inputs elsewhere in the original phase (only weak ~0.15 at t=1), nor on the delimiter or other tokens; precision of the predicate is 1.0. Residual misses are weak (~0.1) activations on the copy-phase step just before a 0 is input, and 0 at t=1. Rate rises with number of digits in the sequence only because 0 is more likely present.

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.918, F1 0.957 and mass recall 0.983. Nothing fires on the delimiter: 0 of 500k active steps on dev.

The 9.7k test misses are weak (about 0.1-0.15) and fall into the minor classes the explanation already names. A 0 input in the original phase at t>=1 covers 4.9% of recall but only 1.1% of mass, with precision 0.23 at t=1 and 0.02 at t>=2. A non-0 copy-phase input just before a 0 covers 2.3% of recall and 0.4% of mass, at precision 0.04. Neither is worth adding to the predicate.
Adding t<=1 to the predicate lowers F1 to 0.923, so the original predicate is the better choice.

The back-to-back 0 claim is consistent with the scores: a 0 after a 0 in the copy phase has precision 1.0 and slightly lower mass per step. The t=0 magnitude of about 0.27-0.30 matches the t=0 mass share (6%).
